enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1143 AM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION, FIRE WEATHER...

.KEY MESSAGES... 
Updated at 1142 AM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

 - Scattered storms will move through northern and western areas
   through this evening with a few storms becoming severe closer
   to the Arizona border. 

 - Better areawide rain chances Thursday and Friday, with isolated
   strong storms and flooding.

 - Temperatures back above normal, with Tuesday through Wednesday 
   being the warmest stretch.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1142 AM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

An active pattern setting up for much of the next week. A
southwest to southerly flow pattern persists at least into Sunday.
This afternoon and evening, we will see a series of disturbances
moving through the region which will help trigger scattered
thunderstorms, primarily west of the RGV, but a few could move
into El Paso and parts of Otero county. There is some good shear
out west with 35-45KTS in the 0-6km layer and CAPE values upwards
of 1000J/kg. Could see a few strong to low end severe. It does
look like it will be more low-topped storms, but with cooler Oct
air in place, hail will be a threat as well as wind. This activity
will move NE through the evening. Overnight lows will be warmer
than last night with higher dew points in place.  

Tue looks like a more down day as we will see some ridging taking
place over the eastern zones and a strong upper low moves slowly
south off the CA coast, but still enough moisture and instability
around to get a few storms over area mountains. Temperatures will
be warming up into the upper 70s to mid 80s for the lowlands. 
Similar conditions continue through the day Wed except as we get 
towards 00Z, there will be some convection developing south of the
Bootheel and pushing north into western CWA. SPC has highlighted 
this area with a marginal severe threat. Shear will definitely be
in place but instability looks marginal.  

Activity starts really ramping up going into Thu and Fri as the
upper low moves onshore, opens up and gets into western MT. The
trough will extend down into the Baja Peninsula and keep a good
moisture fetch from the south and a series of disturbances lining
up. Could see some training through this timeframe and locally
heavy rain. Currently both the GFS and EC Ensemble means support
1-2" over the Gila region with a third to 1" over the lowlands.
Localized areas could see 2-3" by Sat morning.  

Models are in good agreement through Sat morning, but then differ
on how to handle the lingering upper trough. EC continues to be
more progressive and pushing the upper trough east of the area by
Sun morning. GFS has a different solution each run but does want
to keep redeveloping a trough/upper low near the Four Corners
region and precipitation going. The jet pattern seems to favor a
EC solution that is more progressive, but lingering moisture could
keep some isolated to scattered storms over the east going into
Sun. Temperatures as we get into Fri-Sun will cool down with the
trough passage. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(18Z TAFS)
Issued at 1142 AM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

P6SM FEW-SCT060-080 SCT-BKN100-120 through much of the period with
some partial clearing after 06Z. There will be scattered
thunderstorms developing west of the Divide by 21Z and moving
northeast into the evening. Best coverage will be in the Gila
region but as far as impacted terminals, KTCS and KDMN have best
storm chances starting around 00Z with wind gusts over 30KTS and 
even some hail. KLRU and KELP have chances as well but closer to 
02-06Z. Widely scattered showers will continue through the night
similar to last night. Winds generally NE to SE AOB 12KTS. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1142 AM MDT Mon Oct 19 2026

While temperatures will be warming up the next couple of days to
about 10 degrees above normal, fairly high moisture for Oct will
be in place and keep RH's above 30%. There will be scattered
thunderstorms almost daily, especially in area mountains going
into the weekend. Best rain chances come Thu-Fri when some locally
heavy rainfall is possible, especially in the Gila region.
Temperatures will be cooling down as we head into the later part
of the week and rain chances increase. Vent rates generally Fair
to good through Wed. 

&&
